newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil up on physical push.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil up on physical push.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps edged up late afternoon on Friday in trading on expectations of continued physical purchases by a local trader despite the wide East-West spread, traders said.
"The market is staying up because of the physical buying from one trader," a trader said.
March gas oil swaps were last quoted at $26.80/$26.90 per barrel compared with Thursday's $26.60/$26.80. April was quoted at $25.60/$25.70, up from Thrsday's $25.40/$25.50 in thin trading.
The market has so far been support by the large purchases by a Singapore trader who had since the start of last week bought 2.32 million barrels for loading in March and April.
The jet fuel/gas oil spread continued to narrow on Friday as physical jet fuel was traded on Thursday at lower levels, while gas oil were traded at higher levels.

They said gas oil continued to get support from the Singapore trader. The same trader bought large volumes of jet fuel -- the latest being 400,000 barrels on Thursday bringing the total to 1.4 million barrels -- but his purchases were at lower levels.
April traded earlier in the day at $25.70 per barrel, brokers said.
Sources said the market is vulnerable as the East-West spread for April is at a wide $21.50 per tonne and a new round of exports from the looks increasingly likely.
In February a similarly wide arbitrage led to the shipment of more than 500,000-tonnes East with about more than half destined to India.
Traders said a new round of arbitrage exports will most likely send the market southward as regional demand are not large enough to absorb the extra barrels.
As a result the March regrade was offered at 35 cents per barrel, down 35 cents from Thursday, while April was offered at 30 cents, down 10 cents.
Brokers expect swaps regrade to follow the physical market into negative levels soon, as the region enters a low demand period.
Fuel oil swaps were unchanged with March last quoted at $98.00/$99.00 per tonne.
The naphtha market firmed slightly on Japanese enduser demand with April last quoted at $23.40/$23.50, up 15 cents from Thursday.
